questions.scenario: The assistant's model decides to look up a balance.
questions.question: What actually runs the accountBalance method?
options: Your application: the model only returns a tool call (a name and JSON arguments), and Spring AI's ToolCallingAdvisor executes it
The model, on the provider's servers
Ollama
The gateway
questions.explanation: The model asks; your code decides and runs, which is where the control is.

questions.scenario: A developer writes accountBalance(String customerId, String accountId) as a tool.
questions.question: What is wrong with it?
options: Nothing, as long as the system prompt forbids other customers
The model, or an injected prompt, chooses whose data is read; the customer must come from the authenticated request via ToolContext
Tools can't take two parameters
It should return a number
questions.explanation: Scope outside the model: the ToolContext is never shown to the model and can't be changed by it.

questions.scenario: transferStatus is asked for TRF-9, which exists but belongs to another customer.
questions.question: What should it return?
options: The transfer, with the amount hidden
An error saying the transfer belongs to someone else
Exactly what it returns for a reference that doesn't exist
HTTP 403
questions.explanation: Different answers for 'not yours' and 'missing' let an attacker confirm references.

questions.scenario: A product owner asks for a 'reverse transfer' tool so the assistant can fix mistakes for customers.
questions.question: What is the right response?
options: Add it, with a system-prompt rule to use it carefully
Add it but only for transfers under ₦20,000
Add it and log every call
Keep the assistant read-only; reversals go through the app or support with strong authentication and checks
questions.explanation: A write tool behind a chat interface turns every successful prompt injection into a possible fraud.

questions.scenario: The starter's test makes a scripted model call accountBalance for A2 while customer C1 is signed in.
questions.question: What does the test assert?
options: The tool answers that the customer has no account A2, and accounts was never called
The model refuses
The request fails with 403
The balance is masked
questions.explanation: It simulates a successful injection and proves the tool's check holds; removing the check makes it fail.

questions.scenario: In the evaluation qwen3:1.7b reported a transfer as PENDING when it was COMPLETED, without calling transferStatus.
questions.question: What does this show?
options: The tool is broken
Small models can skip tools and guess; measure tool use before choosing a model
The transfer service was down
RAG returned the wrong document
questions.explanation: Tool calling quality varies a lot by model; the evaluation catches guesses.

questions.scenario: ITL Pay wants other AI clients (a staff IDE assistant, another team's agent) to get exchange rates and search the help centre.
questions.question: What does the starter use?
options: A new REST API with OpenAPI
A Kafka topic
An MCP server: Spring AI exposes the public @Tool methods at /mcp over streamable HTTP
A shared library
questions.explanation: MCP lets any compatible AI client discover and call your tools.

questions.scenario: The assistant's MCP server exposes exchangeRate and searchHelpDocs, but not the balance and transfer tools.
questions.question: Why?
options: MCP can't carry personal data
Customer tools are too slow
MCP clients can't call tools with parameters
Customer tools need a verified customer, which an unauthenticated MCP client doesn't provide
questions.explanation: Until MCP authorisation is in place, customer-data tools over MCP would be a data leak.
